concept.name: Market factor
concept.definition: The excess return of the broad value-weighted stock market portfolio over the risk-free rate, the first factor in the CAPM and in all Fama-French models, proxied in the Kenneth French data library by the value-weight return of all eligible CRSP U.S. stocks minus the one-month Treasury bill rate.
concept.intuition: It is simply 'the stock market's return above T-bills' - the baseline common driver that every equity shares and against which other factors are measured.
concept.mechanics: Constructed as Rm - Rf, where Rm is the value-weight return of all CRSP firms incorporated in the U.S. and listed on NYSE/AMEX/NASDAQ with valid share code, price, and return data, and Rf is the one-month T-bill rate; an asset's loading on it is its beta.
concept.formula: MKT_t = Rm_t - Rf_t, with Rm the value-weight market return and Rf the one-month Treasury bill rate.
concept.failure_modes: The theoretical CAPM market portfolio includes all wealth (real estate, human capital), so any tradable index is only a proxy; results can be sensitive to the proxy's universe and weighting.
concept.misconceptions: The market factor is not the raw index return - it is the excess return over the risk-free rate, and it is value-weighted, not equal-weighted, in standard academic construction.
concept.example: If the CRSP value-weight market returns 1.2% in a month and the one-month T-bill yields 0.3%, the market factor realization MKT is 0.9% for that month.

citations.source: Kenneth R. French Data Library, Description of Fama/French Factors
